transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the release package review for 'After the Flood' ahead of the Meridian International Film Festival. I'll need each of you — rights, music, publicity, and accessibility — to walk me through your review of the current draft release sheet before I lock it. I have the draft in front of me: worldwide access, the cue 'Low Tide,' the working title 'River After Rain,' and optional accessibility materials. Let's go through it department by department.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights issue before we go any further. I confirmed with the archive this week that the license for our archival interview permits festival screening and password-protected press access only in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and Ireland. It forbids public online access and access in all other territories. The archive's signed email arrived after the last package revision, so I haven't been able to copy the confirmation into the release sheet yet. This means the current draft's 'worldwide access' listing is not compatible with the license terms.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a music clearance issue with the cue listed on the draft sheet. I confirmed with the publisher that 'Low Tide' — the cue currently listed — is only cleared for 30 seconds. However, the alternate cue 'Northbound' is cleared for the full 46-second trailer segment. I haven't replaced the cue name in the package yet because the editor delivered the latest cut after my clearance check, so the draft still shows 'Low Tide.' We'll need to update the cue to 'Northbound' before the package is locked.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: On the publicity side, I need to flag a title and credit issue. I have the filmmaker's signed publicity approval, which requires the title 'After the Flood' and the credit line 'A film by Nia Okafor.' The working title 'River After Rain' and the generic credit are still in the draft because the signed approval arrived during the poster revision, so I haven't been able to update the release sheet yet. We'll need to correct both the title and the credit line before the package is locked.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical accessibility issue. I confirmed with the festival's access coordinator that the final submission must include open English captions and a separate audio-description track. The coordinator will reject a package containing either deliverable as optional. This requirement came through in a separate accessibility email from the festival, so I haven't updated the release checklist yet. The current draft lists accessibility materials as optional, which does not meet the festival's ingest requirement. We'll need to make both open English captions and the audio-description track mandatory deliverables before the package is locked.
transcript.speaker: A5
